candidates.topic: Cleopatra's needle obelisk hidden time capsule
candidates.teaser: There's a hidden chamber inside a famous landmark that almost no one knows about — and what's inside will surprise you.
candidates.video_title: The Secret Box Buried Under the Statue of Liberty
candidates.video_description: The Statue of Liberty holds a hidden time capsule that most people have never heard of. Sealed inside its foundation are artifacts from 1884 that tell a fascinating story. What would you put in a time capsule for the next century?
candidates.script: The Statue of Liberty has a secret almost nobody talks about. When workers laid the cornerstone in 1884, they sealed a copper box inside the foundation — filled with coins, a copy of the Declaration of Independence, and even newspaper clippings from the day. It has never been opened since. The statue standing above it has turned green from weather and time, but that box is still sitting in the dark, perfectly preserved, waiting. The real question is — if they open it tomorrow, what do you think they'd find in the best condition?

candidates.teaser: Scientists are seriously planning to bring back an animal that went extinct thousands of years ago — and they're closer than you think.
candidates.video_title: Scientists Are Actually Bringing Back the Woolly Mammoth
candidates.video_description: A biotech company called Colossal Biosciences is actively working to resurrect the woolly mammoth using ancient DNA and CRISPR gene editing. Their target date is closer than most people realize. Could de-extinction change how we think about nature forever?
candidates.script: Scientists are literally trying to bring back the woolly mammoth — and this isn't science fiction. A company called Colossal Biosciences has extracted ancient mammoth DNA from frozen remains preserved in Siberian permafrost for over ten thousand years. Using CRISPR gene editing, they're splicing mammoth traits into elephant embryos — cold resistance, thick fur, extra fat layers. Their goal is to have living mammoth-like creatures walking the tundra by 2028. The idea is that they'd actually help slow climate change by restoring the Arctic ecosystem. But here's what nobody is asking — what happens if it works a little too well?

candidates.topic: Humans replace entire skeleton every decade
candidates.teaser: The body you were born with is almost entirely gone — and science can prove exactly when it disappeared.
candidates.video_title: Your Skeleton Is Not the One You Were Born With
candidates.video_description: Your bones feel permanent and solid, but they are constantly being broken down and rebuilt at a cellular level. Every decade, your entire skeleton has been completely replaced. The body you have now is a different physical structure than the one you had ten years ago.
candidates.script: The skeleton inside you right now is not the one you were born with. Your bones feel rock solid and permanent, but they are constantly being demolished and rebuilt by specialized cells called osteoblasts and osteoclasts — working around the clock like microscopic construction crews. By the time you're ten years older, every single bone in your body has been completely replaced, atom by atom. The calcium in your femur today might have been part of your spine just a few years ago. So technically, you and your skeleton from ten years ago are strangers. Does that mean the you from a decade ago is actually... gone?

candidates.topic: The longest lightning bolt ever recorded
candidates.teaser: One single bolt of lightning once crossed an area larger than most countries — and someone actually measured it.
candidates.video_title: The Lightning Bolt That Crossed an Entire Country
candidates.video_description: In 2020, a single lightning bolt was officially recorded stretching over 768 kilometers across the southern United States — wider than most European countries. The World Meteorological Organization certified it as the longest lightning flash in recorded history. Lightning is far more powerful and vast than most people ever imagine.
candidates.script: In April 2020, a single bolt of lightning stretched 768 kilometers across the southern United States — that's wider than the entire country of France. The World Meteorological Organization officially certified it as the longest lightning flash ever recorded in human history. Scientists call these rare events megaflashes, and they happen when the electrical charge inside storm systems reaches such an extreme level that it just keeps jumping across the sky, refusing to stop. One bolt. Nearly 800 kilometers. Gone in less than a second. Now consider this — if you were standing at one end, the other end of that lightning bolt would be completely over the horizon. How small does that make you feel?

candidates.teaser: The entire internet has a physical weight — and the number will genuinely surprise you.
candidates.video_title: The Entire Internet Has a Physical Weight
candidates.video_description: Every email, video, and website that exists on the internet is stored as electrons, and electrons have mass. Scientists have actually calculated the approximate physical weight of all the data on the internet. The answer is almost insultingly small — and that makes it even more mind-blowing.
candidates.script: The entire internet — every video, every message, every website that has ever existed — physically weighs something. Because all digital data is stored as electrons, and electrons have real measurable mass, scientists have actually calculated it. The total weight of the internet is roughly 50 grams — about the same as a single strawberry. All of human knowledge, every movie ever uploaded, every text ever sent, lighter than the fruit in your fridge. The wild part is that as the internet grows with more data every second, it technically gets heavier. So right now, while you're watching this — you just made the internet a tiny bit heavier.
